questions.question: Which process breaks rock into smaller pieces without changing its composition?
Which example is chemical weathering?
choices: A rock split by ice expansion
Rock broken by a falling tree
Minerals dissolving in mildly acidic water

questions.question: What is abrasion?
choices: Wearing surfaces through scraping by moving particles

questions.question: What is mass wasting?
choices: Downslope movement of rock or soil under gravity
A river carrying dissolved ions uphill
The loss of atomic mass during weathering

questions.question: What is a river delta?
choices: A crack formed by plate collision
A mountain formed only by lava
A sediment deposit where a river enters quieter water
A channel carved entirely by a glacier

questions.question: Which process deposits wind-carried sand into dunes?
What is soil?
choices: A pure mineral with one formula
A mixture of mineral material, organic matter, water, air, and organisms

questions.question: How can freezing water contribute to rock breakdown?
choices: Freezing turns every rock into limestone
Water in cracks expands as it freezes and can widen them
Water becomes denser and contracts in every freezing crack

questions.question: Why can plant roots contribute to mechanical weathering?
choices: Plants remove gravity from the soil
Growing roots can exert pressure within cracks

questions.question: Why does faster-flowing water generally transport larger sediment particles?
choices: It can exert greater force on particles
It stops all small particles moving
It converts gravel into dissolved gas

questions.question: Why is sediment often deposited when a river slows?
choices: Reduced transport capacity allows particles to settle
Slower water creates new sediment atoms
Gravity stops acting on moving water
The particles become more soluble automatically

questions.question: How can vegetation reduce soil erosion?
choices: Roots make every soil particle heavier than bedrock
Roots hold soil, and plant cover reduces surface impacts and runoff

questions.question: Why does chemical weathering often proceed faster in warm, moist climates?
choices: Water availability and temperature favor many weathering reactions
Cold, dry air always supplies more liquid water

questions.question: What is one reason angular rock fragments may become rounded during river transport?
choices: Their elements change into lighter elements
All grains melt in river water
Collisions and abrasion wear their edges

questions.question: How does human removal of plant cover often affect erosion risk?
choices: It exposes soil to greater wind and water transport
It removes the influence of slope

questions.question: A rock develops cracks after repeated wetting and freezing. Which mechanism best fits?
Coarse grains settle before finer suspended grains when a stream slows. What explains this sorting?
choices: All grains have identical settling behavior
The stream creates new mineral species
Fine grains must always have greater mass
Particle size affects settling and transport behavior

questions.question: A steep saturated slope moves downhill after heavy rain. Which process is most directly illustrated?
A river enters a lake and builds a fan-shaped deposit near its mouth. Which feature is developing?
Two similar fields lie on equal slopes. One retains crop cover; one is left bare. Which generally has greater erosion risk during heavy rain?
choices: Both must lose exactly equal soil
